questions.question: For a discrete random variable, how is support described?
options: As the set of values with positive mass
As the set of values where a density is negative
As the whole real line in every case
As only the expected value

questions.question: For a continuous random variable, how is support often described?
options: Through where the density is positive
Through the values with positive point mass only
Through the order of outcomes in $S$
Through the number of generated events

questions.question: Why is support not the same as the full distribution?
options: Support says where probability lies, not how much lies there
Support lists the probabilities too, so it fixes the distribution
They differ only for continuous variables, where points have probability zero
Support is always an interval, while distributions can be discrete

questions.question: If a die-roll variable has support $\{1,\ldots,6\}$, what is the probability of value $8$ under the model?
Let $X\sim\operatorname{Bern}(p)$ with $0\le p\le1$. For which $p$ is the support of $X$ equal to $\{0,1\}$?
options: Exactly when $0<p<1$
For every $p\in[0,1]$
Only when $p=\frac{1}{2}$
Exactly when $p\in\{0,1\}$

questions.question: Let $X\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)$ with density $1$ on $(0,1)$ and $0$ elsewhere. Is $0$ in the topological support of $X$?
options: Yes; $\mathbb{P}(|X|<\varepsilon)>0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$
No; the density is $0$ at the point $0$
No; $\mathbb{P}(X=0)=0$
Only if the density is redefined to be $1$ at $0$

questions.question: A random variable $X$ has the continuous CDF $F$ with $F(x)=0$ for $x<0$, $F(x)=\frac{x}{4}$ for $0\le x<2$, $F(x)=\frac{1}{2}$ for $2\le x<4$, $F(x)=\frac{x}{4}-\frac{1}{2}$ for $4\le x<6$ and $F(x)=1$ for $x\ge6$. What is the topological support $\{x\colon\mathbb{P}(|X-x|<\varepsilon)>0\text{ for every }\varepsilon>0\}$ of $X$?
options: $(0,\infty)$

questions.question: A random variable $X$ takes the value $\frac{1}{n}$ with probability $2^{-n}$ for each $n=1,2,3,\dots$ What is the topological support $\{x\colon\mathbb{P}(|X-x|<\varepsilon)>0\text{ for every }\varepsilon>0\}$ of $X$?
options: $\{\frac{1}{n}\colon n\ge1\}\cup\{0\}$
$\{\frac{1}{n}\colon n\ge1\}$
